description: real DBLP records (original bytes, ISO-8859-1): the 50 records of selection-10k with the smallest sha256(seed|key), in dump order
rule: Eligibility (fixed order, first failing reason counted): (1) top-level record type is article or inproceedings; (2) key attribute present and non-empty; (3) key unique among all top-level records in the dump; (4) title text (all character data inside <title>, inline markup flattened, entities resolved) non-empty after trimming; (5) first <year> is all ASCII digits; (6) at least 2 <author> children; (7) at least one <ee> whose value is an http(s)://[www.][dx.]doi.org/ URL (else no_doi_org_ee); (8) for the first such <ee> in document order yielding a valid DOI: canonical DOI = strip URL prefix, percent-decode, trim, lowercase; it must start with '10.' and contain no whitespace (else doi_invalid). DOI de-duplication: among eligible records sharing a canonical DOI, keep only the record with the smallest rank (rank = sha256(seed + '|' + key) hex); the others leave the pool. Selection: for each size N, allocate N across publication years in proportion to the de-duplicated pool counts using the largest-remainder method (remainder ties broken by ascending year); each smaller size is additionally capped per year by the allocation of the next larger size. Within each year take the a(year) records with the smallest rank. Never 'first N records'. Smaller selections are subsets of larger ones.
sample_rule: n smallest sha256(seed + '|' + key) among selection-10k keys
